primitives.name: Dependency Tree Risk Quantifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: The dominant risk is NOT app logic — it is the dependency tree: next-auth/@auth/core carry 2 CRITICAL advisories (homoglyph email bypass; fail-open auth object), next has a deserialization DoS, and the build chain (postcss) has an arbitrary-file-read advisory.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{dep}': 'dimensionless risk score of dependency tree', 'A_{crit}': 'count of critical advisories', 'A_{high}': 'count of high advisories'}
primitives.assumptions: Risk scales linearly with number of unresolved advisories; auth stack failure implies system-wide compromise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When A_{crit} > 0, system enters unstable regime due to auth bypass.

layer2.mapping: The dependency tree's vulnerability profile mirrors the system's authentication failure probability distribution.
layer2.telemetry: npm audit result counts and patch status

primitives.name: Authentication Stack Integrity Monitor
primitives.verbatim_quote: CRITICAL — next-auth/@auth/core advisories (homoglyph email bypass, fail-open auth object) — auth stack, unpatched.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I_{auth}': 'integrity indicator of auth stack (0 to 1)', 'P_{failopen}': 'probability of fail-open condition', 'P_{bypass}': 'probability of homoglyph bypass'}
primitives.assumptions: Auth stack integrity degrades when unresolved advisories exceed threshold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If I_{auth} < 0.5, system is vulnerable to unauthorized admin access.

layer2.mapping: Auth integrity is derived from the resolution state of core dependency advisories.
layer2.telemetry: Patch version of @auth/core and audit results

primitives.name: API Route Exposure Tracker
primitives.verbatim_quote: risks: rate limiting covers a small fraction of API routes, CSP allows unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval, and three pre-existing tracked-debt failures keep CI red (model-freeze #419, api-v1-boundary #420, typecheck #421) — all documented, none caused by this branch.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_{route}': 'exposure level of API routes (0 to 1)', 'L_{limit}': 'fraction of routes under rate limit', 'D_{debt}': 'count of tracked governance debts'}
primitives.assumptions: Exposure increases with fewer rate-limited routes and higher governance debt.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When E_{route} > 0.7, system is exposed to DoS or unauthorized access.

layer2.mapping: Route exposure is derived from rate-limit coverage and governance debt metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Number of rate-limited routes and open governance issues

reasoning_traces.think:
The audit identifies two primary failure modes: dependency tree instability and auth stack compromise. Dependency risk R_dep is modeled as a function of critical advisories A_crit and high severity findings A_high. Auth integrity I_auth is a derived quantity dependent on patch resolution of @auth/core. Exposure E_route is a composite of rate-limit coverage L_limit and governance debt D_debt. These primitives form a triadic risk space where each dimension interacts: unresolved dependencies increase auth failure probability, which in turn increases route exposure. The system's stability hinges on maintaining I_auth > 0.5 and E_route < 0.7. Temporal consistency of npm audit results validates these mappings, confirming that patch resolution resolves critical risks. The dual nature of these primitives—structural (dependency) and behavioral (auth/integrity)—reflects the duality between static codebase risk and dynamic runtime behavior.
